Ceci est le premier d’une série d’articles sur le « Discipulat ». Aujourd’hui, Jésus continue d’appeler des hommes et des femmes à répondre au simple appel : « Suis-moi ». Jésus appelle chacun de nous à personnellement « Le suivre ». Dans cette série, nous explorerons la profondeur de ce simple commandement de Jésus. Comme les disciples, vous vous trouverez attiré à suivre Jésus.

Vous pouvez ressentir à la fois de l’exaltation et de l’appréhension. De l’exaltation, alors que votre parcours de foi vous mène vers des sommets d’amour que vous n’avez jamais connus. De l’appréhension, alors que votre foi est éprouvée de manières nouvelles et difficiles.

Il y a un vide dans chaque cœur humain que seul Jésus peut remplir. Il y a une pureté et une beauté dans la vie de Jésus qui résonnent avec ces désirs du cœur. En marchant avec Jésus, nous nous retrouvons transformés. Les choses anciennes passent. Toutes choses deviennent nouvelles. Sa vie devient notre vie. Ses désirs deviennent nos désirs.

Le discipulat incombe au croyant. Croire en Jésus, se repentir de nos péchés et recevoir le Seigneur Jésus dans notre cœur sont les premiers pas d’un voyage de foi qui dure toute la vie. Le discipulat n’est pas un moyen alternatif de salut. Suivre Jésus est la réponse d’une âme affranchie. Suivre Jésus n’est pas une tentative charnelle de mériter la vie éternelle. C’est la réponse d’amour de celui qui a découvert la source de la vie.

Si vous vous joignez à nous dans ce voyage, vous découvrirez que suivre Jésus nous conduira dans la vallée de la décision où nous nous trouverons contraints de choisir entre une vie de totale abandon à Christ ou une vie de péché et de satisfaction de soi.

Et Jésus, marchant près de la mer de Galilée, vit deux frères, Simon appelé Pierre, et André son frère, qui jetaient un filet dans la mer; car ils étaient pêcheurs. Et il leur dit: Suivez-moi, et je vous ferai pêcheurs d’hommes. Aussitôt ils laissèrent leurs filets, et le suivirent. Et étant allé de là, il vit deux autres frères, Jacques, fils de Zébédée, et Jean son frère, qui étaient dans une barque avec Zébédée leur père, raccommodant leurs filets; et il les appela. Et aussitôt ils laissèrent la barque et leur père, et le suivirent –Matthew 4:18-22.

Imaginez-vous dans une barque avec l’un de ces frères. Le soleil se levait à l’horizon oriental. En prévision d’une autre journée de pêche sur les eaux bleues de la Galilée, vous vous affairiez aux tâches quotidiennes. La pêche a été votre vie. Vous êtes aussi à l’aise en mer que dans votre chaumière.

Un autre jour, une autre prise de poissons, et vous devriez pouvoir tenir les créanciers à distance pour une semaine de plus. C’est la seule vie que vous ayez jamais connue. Votre père était pêcheur. Votre grand-père était pêcheur. C’est une vie confortable. C’est une vie familière.

Ce matin, alors que les vagues clapotaient doucement sur le rivage sablonneux, un homme s’approche. Il n’est pas un parfait inconnu. Tout le monde connaît le fils de Marie. Chacun a une opinion sur le fils de Marie. Il étonne le rabbin local par sa connaissance des Écritures. Son caractère est sans faille; il est l’ami de tous et l’étranger de personne.

Cet homme, Jésus (c’est son nom) s’approche de votre barque. En s’approchant, il appelle d’une voix plutôt joyeuse: « Suivez-moi. »

Jacques regarde Jean, et ensemble ils regardent leur père Zébédée. Son hochement de tête approbateur était tout ce dont ils avaient besoin. Zébédée avait travaillé avec ses deux fils pendant de nombreuses années. Peut-être espérait-il que le temps passé avec le Nazaréen adoucirait le tempérament de leurs caractères abrasifs.

« Suivez-moi, et je vous ferai pêcheurs d’hommes. » C’est ce qu’il cria à Pierre et André. Ils quittèrent leur petite barque pleine de filets, peut-être attachée à une souche sur le rivage. Qu’avait cet homme pour pouvoir attirer des disciples derrière lui avec un simple « Suivez-moi » ? Peut-être y avait-il un profond désir dans le cœur de ces disciples — un « espoir » que suivre Jésus pourrait s’accomplir.

Des générations d’hommes juifs avaient cherché le Messie — le Promis; Celui qui briserait le joug romain et rendrait à Israël sa liberté et sa gloire passées. Jésus était la perspective révolutionnaire la plus prometteuse de l’époque. Il aurait besoin d’un entourage. Il aurait besoin de leur aide. Ils ne se rendaient pas compte ce jour-là, en laissant tomber leurs filets et en suivant Jésus, où ce voyage les mènerait. Ils ne savaient pas qu’en suivant cet homme, ils ne seraient plus jamais les mêmes.

Lorsque Pierre, André, Jacques et Jean se joignirent à huit autres pour suivre Jésus, ils s’éloignaient de la vie familière et sûre du pêcheur. Ils ont peut-être pensé que suivre Jésus serait une aventure. Ils ont peut-être pensé qu’après une période de service auprès du Nazaréen, ils pourraient retourner à leurs barques. En fait, c’est ce qu’ils firent.

Après la crucifixion et la résurrection de Jésus, il fit plusieurs apparitions à ses disciples. Ils n’avaient pas encore reçu le Saint-Esprit, et, au milieu de cette grande incertitude, ils ne purent résister à l’attrait du familier. Ils décidèrent d’aller pêcher, mais à leur grand désarroi ils avaient perdu le coup de main. Ils pêchèrent toute la nuit et ne prirent rien. Le matin, Jésus se tenait sur le rivage. Il leur dit de jeter du côté droit de la barque. Ils jetèrent et ne purent remonter les filets à cause de la multitude de poissons.

Simon Pierre leur dit: Je vais pêcher. Ils lui disent: Nous allons aussi avec toi. Ils sortirent, et montèrent dans la barque aussitôt; et cette nuit-là ils ne prirent rien. Mais quand le matin fut venu, Jésus se tenait sur le rivage; et les disciples ne savaient pas que c’était Jésus. Alors Jésus leur dit: Enfants, avez-vous du poisson? Ils lui répondirent: Non. Et il leur dit: Jetez le filet du côté droit de la barque, et vous trouverez. Ils le jetèrent donc, et maintenant ils ne pouvaient le remonter à cause de la multitude des poissons –John 21:3-6.

Vous êtes-vous déjà trouvé dans une situation où vous avez essayé et essayé et où tous vos efforts se sont soldés par un échec ? Vous savez ce que c’est que « d’atteindre la fin de mes ressources accumulées ». Si c’est là où vous vous trouvez, vous êtes en position d’expérimenter un miracle. Dieu se montre fort envers ceux qui reconnaissent leur faiblesse.

Quand vous décidez de suivre Jésus, il vous attirera dans une dépendance telle à son égard que vous ne compterez finalement plus sur vous-même. Devenir véritablement semblable à Jésus, c’est réaliser avec Paul …que, dans moi (c’est-à-dire dans ma chair,) il n’y a rien de bon… Paul continue alors le verset …car vouloir est présent en moi; mais comment accomplir ce qui est bon, je le trouve pas –Romans 7:18.

Le discipulat nous conduira à un abandon total de nous-mêmes à Christ. Tout comme les disciples n’auraient pas pu imaginer où les mènerait le fait de suivre Jésus, nous non plus. Nous faisons un choix de foi. Nous choisissons de suivre. Nous remettons les détails à notre Maître.

Si vous voulez être comme Jésus, vous ne pouvez pas regarder en arrière. Jésus a dit: …Personne, ayant mis la main à la charrue, et regardant en arrière, n’est propre pour le royaume de Dieu –Luke 9:62. Pierre regarda en arrière. Il dit: « Je vais pêcher ». Désabusé après la crucifixion et la glorieuse résurrection, Pierre choisit de retourner au mode de vie qui lui était familier. Il retourna à la pêche et Jacques et Jean le suivirent.

Quand Jésus apparut sur le rivage après leur longue nuit de labeur sans fruit, il prépara une friture de poissons pour les disciples fatigués. Alors que Pierre grignotait un poisson grillé, Jésus se tourna vers lui et dit : « Pierre, m’aimes-tu plus que ceux-ci ? » Que ces paroles de Jésus sont doucement pénétrantes.

Pierre répondit : « Oui Seigneur, tu sais que je t’aime. » Jésus dit : « Pais mes agneaux. » Nous ne savons pas combien de temps s’est écoulé, mais Jésus se tourna à nouveau vers lui, « Pierre… » (en fait il l’appela Simon) « M’aimes-tu ? » Pierre donna la même réponse posée. « Oui Seigneur, tu sais que je t’aime. » C’était la bonne réponse, mais Jésus cherchait plus qu’une simple bonne réponse, alors il lui dit encore : « Simon, fils de Jonas, m’aimes-tu ? »

Pierre commença enfin à sentir que Jésus lui demandait quelque chose de plus — quelque chose qui perçait son âme au plus profond. Il avait commencé à suivre Jésus avec le désir de recevoir de lui. Maintenant Jésus lui demande de réciproquer cet amour.

Les scènes de la maison de Caïphe lui revinrent. Il vit Jésus être brutalement maltraité, faussement accusé et craché dessus. Il entendit les cris furieux du sanhédrin appelant à la mort de Jésus. Et puis il y eut cette jeune servante insistante qui l’accusa d’être l’un des disciples de Jésus. Il lui dit: « Je ne suis pas ». Trois fois il avait renié connaître Jésus et maintenant trois fois Jésus a mis au défi son amour.

Dans l’angoisse du cœur, Pierre s’écria : « Seigneur, tu sais toutes choses; tu sais que je t’aime ». Jésus lui dit : « Fais paître mes brebis ». Dès ce jour, Pierre fut un homme avec un appel, non seulement pour connaître Christ dans le but de recevoir de lui, mais aussi pour l’imiter. Le discipulat, c’est plus que simplement connaître Jésus. Le discipulat, c’est marcher dans ses pas et s’identifier à Jésus dans son ministère et dans ses souffrances — le connaître véritablement.

Jésus te demande aujourd’hui : « M’aimes-tu ? » Nous connaissons tous la bonne réponse, « Oui, bien sûr, j’aime Jésus. » Ensuite « Aime ton prochain » – « Sert les nécessiteux » – « Cède devant ton frère » – « Pardonne à celui qui t’a offensé ».

Le discipulat est très pratique en ce sens qu’il nous pousse au-delà de l’idéologique et nous fait devenir les mains et les pieds mêmes de Jésus pour ceux qui nous entourent.

Si dans ton cœur tu penses, cela ne semble pas très attrayant, je t’encourage à te concentrer sur le moment et sur la tâche à accomplir. Pierre marcha avec Jésus pendant trois ans et demi avant de recevoir cet appel de Jésus. Jésus ne nous appelle jamais sans nous équiper, et il ne nous équipe pas avant d’avoir jugé que nous sommes prêts. Après la journée de la Pentecôte, Pierre fut appelé, préparé et équipé. Alors Dieu l’utilisa puissamment pour établir l’Église.

Je voudrais attirer ton attention sur un autre attribut du discipulat qui est parfois mal placé. Le discipulat n’est jamais destiné à être de la corvée. Si tu trouves que suivre Jésus est dur et pénible, cela prouve que ton amour n’a pas encore été parfait.

La question qui transperça l’âme que Jésus posa à Pierre était très simple, « M’aimes-tu ? » C’était comme si Jésus mettait Pierre à l’épreuve. [« J’ai un travail pour toi, Pierre, mais une condition préalable à ce travail est ton amour dévoué pour moi. »] Le discipulat est une réponse d’amour à Jésus. Notre amour pour Christ rend le service une joie. Le labeur devient agréable et le sacrifice n’est pas une perte.

Nous pouvons mieux comprendre cela dans le contexte des relations humaines. Si tu es marié et que tu aimes vraiment ton mari ou ta femme, tu ne considères même pas comme un sacrifice de travailler pour le bénéfice mutuel de ton mariage. De la même manière, si nous aimons réellement Jésus, il n’est pas considéré comme une corvée de travailler pour lui. Aucun sacrifice que nous faisons pour le royaume des cieux n’est une perte.

Je te convie à nous rejoindre tandis que nous explorons les réalités du discipulat. Nous apprendrons de l’exemple de Christ en matière de pardon. Nous acquerrons une compréhension plus grande de ce que signifie marcher par la foi. Jésus nous a enseigné à ne pas nous inquiéter mais à faire confiance. Il a enseigné des leçons sur le leadership serviteur et sur le port de la croix. Il y a tant à découvrir quand nous marchons avec Jésus.

Attends-toi à être changé. Les enseignements de Jésus sont révolutionnaires en ce qu’ils vont à l’encontre de nos impulsions humaines. Aie pour but de permettre à la vie du Christ de devenir ta vie et tu seras étonné de ce que Dieu fera pour toi.

There is coming a day when all will be well.
The things that are bad will all be in hell.
But we must not forget that day has not come.
We are in a battle; we must still overcome.
The enemy rages, his time here is short.
He spreads all his lies, the truth to distort.
Sin in our lives, it is his great goal.
For he knows very well it will cost us our soul.
It need not be big; a small sin will do.
He’ll trick and deceive, each soul to pursue.
The darts of the wicked come from all sides.
When faced with God’s power, that devil—he hides!
When God is with us, he cannot advance!
When God is with us, sin has no chance!
For the eyes of the Lord seek to and fro,
To find one perfect, His power He’ll show!
Let’s be done with the lesser and look far beyond.
Let’s take hold of God’s power! It’s time to respond!

Greetings of love in the blessed name of our Lord and Savior, Jesus Christ. Many Christians have gone through a time of trial and testing during the past several years, yet we trust that each one is able to say with Paul… Not that I speak in respect of want: for I have learned, in whatsoever state I am, therewith to be content –Philippians 4:11.

Summer is hard upon us, along with the heat and humidity that goes along with summers here in Ohio. Springtime, along with the normal planting season, was extra long and drawn out. But, by now, most of what is known locally as “the spring work” has been finished. The farmers’ crops and the gardeners’ herbs are pushing through the cool soil and towards the heat and light of the sun.

In this issue you can take a stroll on the road to Emmaus and try to put yourself in the sandals of Jesus’ disciples as they puzzled over the sudden turn of events surrounding Christ’s death, burial, and alleged “resurrection”. You can try to picture yourself with Daniel of old as he chose to keep praying like normal at his open window, while knowing full well that this simple act most likely could change his life forever. You can marvel with little “Ellie” how God met the “desires of her heart” even before she knew things weren’t working out according to plan.

Something new in this issue is the beginning of a series by Brother Donald Brechbill on “discipleship”. Disciple has almost the same spelling as discipline. For many, discipline carries a negative connotation, which hopefully will not interfere with the reader being drawn to what Brother Donald has to share. Let’s remember that Jesus gave personal example of the discipleship model—He chose and called “disciples” to follow and learn from Him. Later He sent them out two by two to teach and make more disciples. And then when He gave the “Great Commission” it was to His disciples at that time, and to all future disciples—the Church of Jesus Christ. We trust that each one can be inspired by this series.

Coming up in future issues, we are planning to have a “Song of the Quarter” and a section on various aspects of “Church History”. You can pray for us as we continue to move forward with our ministry and our magazine.

Just a friendly reminder… We encourage feedback from our readers. If you have been especially blessed by a certain article, feedback is helpful for us as a board, and it is encouraging for our writers. Also, if there is something specific that someone wishes to see included in future magazine issues, we welcome the input. This helps provide ideas for us as a board when choosing articles and when asking authors to write.

In the spring of 2022, we made some changes with our ministry in our endeavors to keep the work of The Berean Voice moving forward into the future. Personnel changes:

Brother Andrew (our designer) has become increasingly busy as a young father with a growing family and as a deacon for our local church congregation. In looking at this challenge, the board decided to support Andrew’s desire to find someone to help him (for now) with the bulk of the design work for each issue of our magazine—The Heartbeat of the Remnant. Thus, there may be some slight changes in the “style” of design in upcoming issues.

In the spring of 2022, there was a decision to seek several new board members to replace several others who had quit over the last number of years due to personal responsibilities. After praying for the Lord’s wisdom and direction, and after consultation with the leadership of our church, Brother Joe Mast and Brother Sheldon Bower were chosen to fill the empty slots on the board. These brothers have both graciously accepted this calling and are already allowing God to use their spiritual gifts to make a difference

Brother Joe Tindall has been a board member for The Berean Voice since our beginning in June of 2016. Due to his age (83) Brother Joe asked to be relieved of his duties as a board member. At our monthly board meeting in May of 2022, the board honored Brother Joe’s request. We will miss the stability of his quiet wisdom in our board meetings and during our article selection process. Please join us in prayer for Brother Joe and his family as he and his wife face the end of their lives and all that goes along with that season of life—that they might remain faithful and courageous.

May God bless and keep each one.

Curvin L Wenger

Saludos de amor en el bendito nombre de nuestro Señor y Salvador, Jesucristo. Muchos cristianos han pasado por un tiempo de prueba y puesta a prueba durante los últimos años, sin embargo confiamos en que cada uno puede decir con Pablo… No lo digo porque tenga escasez; pues he aprendido a contentarme, cualquiera que sea mi situación —Filipenses 4:11.

El verano está encima de nosotros, junto con el calor y la humedad que acompañan los veranos aquí en Ohio. La primavera, junto con la temporada normal de siembra, fue especialmente larga y prolongada. Pero, a estas alturas, la mayor parte de lo que aquí se conoce como "el trabajo de primavera" ya ha terminado. Los cultivos de los agricultores y las hierbas de los jardineros están abriéndose paso a través del suelo frío y hacia el calor y la luz del sol.

En este número puedes dar un paseo por el camino de Emaús e intentar ponerte en las sandalias de los discípulos de Jesús mientras se intrigaban por el giro repentino de los acontecimientos en torno a la muerte, sepultura y supuesta "resurrección" de Cristo. Puedes intentar imaginarte con el antiguo Daniel mientras elegía seguir orando como de costumbre en su ventana abierta, sabiendo muy bien que este simple acto probablemente podría cambiar su vida para siempre. Puedes asombrarte con la pequeña "Ellie" de cómo Dios satisfizo los "deseos de su corazón" incluso antes de que ella supiera que las cosas no estaban saliendo según lo planeado.

Algo nuevo en este número es el comienzo de una serie del hermano Donald Brechbill sobre la "discipulado". Disciple tiene casi la misma ortografía que discipline. Para muchos, discipline tiene una connotación negativa, la cual, esperanzadamente, no interferirá con que el lector se sienta atraído por lo que el hermano Donald tiene para compartir. Recordemos que Jesús dio ejemplo personal del modelo de discipulado: Él eligió y llamó a "discípulos" para que lo siguieran y aprendieran de Él. Más tarde los envió de dos en dos para enseñar y hacer más discípulos. Y cuando Él dio la "Gran Comisión", fue a sus discípulos en ese momento, y a todos los futuros discípulos—la Iglesia de Jesucristo. Confiamos en que cada lector pueda inspirarse con esta serie.

En próximos números, planeamos tener una "Canción del Trimestre" y una sección sobre varios aspectos de la "Historia de la Iglesia". Pueden orar por nosotros mientras continuamos avanzando con nuestro ministerio y nuestra revista.

Un recordatorio amistoso... Animamos a los lectores a enviar comentarios. Si un artículo en particular te ha bendecido especialmente, los comentarios son útiles para nosotros como junta, y son un estímulo para nuestros escritores. Además, si hay algo específico que alguien desee ver incluido en futuros números de la revista, damos la bienvenida a la opinión. Esto ayuda a proporcionar ideas para nosotros como junta al elegir artículos y al pedir a los autores que escriban.

En la primavera de 2022, hicimos algunos cambios en nuestro ministerio en nuestros esfuerzos por mantener el trabajo de The Berean Voice avanzando hacia el futuro. Cambios de personal:

El hermano Andrew (nuestro diseñador) se ha vuelto cada vez más ocupado como joven padre con una familia en crecimiento y como diácono de nuestra congregación local. Al enfrentar este desafío, la junta decidió apoyar el deseo de Andrew de encontrar a alguien que le ayude (por ahora) con la mayor parte del trabajo de diseño de cada número de nuestra revista—The Heartbeat of the Remnant. Por lo tanto, puede haber algunos cambios leves en el "estilo" de diseño en los próximos números.

En la primavera de 2022, se tomó la decisión de buscar varios nuevos miembros de la junta para reemplazar a varios otros que habían renunciado durante los últimos años debido a responsabilidades personales. Después de orar por la sabiduría y dirección del Señor, y tras consulta con el liderazgo de nuestra iglesia, el hermano Joe Mast y el hermano Sheldon Bower fueron escogidos para llenar los puestos vacantes en la junta. Estos hermanos han aceptado con gracia este llamado y ya están permitiendo que Dios use sus dones espirituales para hacer la diferencia

El hermano Joe Tindall ha sido miembro de la junta de The Berean Voice desde nuestros comienzos en junio de 2016. Debido a su edad (83), el hermano Joe pidió ser relevado de sus deberes como miembro de la junta. En nuestra reunión mensual de la junta en mayo de 2022, la junta honró la petición del hermano Joe. Extrañaremos la estabilidad de su serena sabiduría en nuestras reuniones de junta y durante nuestro proceso de selección de artículos. Por favor, únanse a nosotros en oración por el hermano Joe y su familia mientras él y su esposa enfrentan el final de sus vidas y todo lo que conlleva esa etapa de la vida—para que permanezcan fieles y valientes.

Que Dios bendiga y guarde a cada uno.

Curvin L Wenger

Around the world, but particularly in the United States, people seem to value rugged individualism. People who demonstrate this character quality make their own way through life, asking nothing from others and expecting nothing.

I suppose that this idea relates back to the pioneers. These were men and women who trekked across the various new countries looking for a place where they could settle down and call home. There were few general stores and as much as possible they lived as self-sufficiently as they could.

While this may sound like a scenario that demonstrates strength, the truth is somewhat different these days. These days people use technology to deliberately create bubbles of isolation around themselves.

Many older people have found themselves increasingly isolated from friends and family. COVID certainly made this worse, but there were seeds of this seclusion that had been sowed long before COVID was ever heard of.

Isolation is Not a Natural State

Looking back to the Garden of Eden we can see that Adam was created before Eve. While there were lots of animals around, there was no true companionship for Adam. And the LORD God said, It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him … And Adam gave names to all cattle, and to the fowl of the air, and to every beast of the field; but for Adam there was not found an help meet for him –Genesis 2:18-20.

And the LORD God caused a deep sleep to fall upon Adam, and he slept: and he took one of his ribs, and closed up the flesh instead thereof; And the rib, which the LORD God had taken from man, made he a woman, and brought her unto the man –Genesis 2:21-22. Of course, this was the beginning of marriage, but the more important thing to see here is that it is not a normal state for humans to be alone. We desire companionship and not just the companionship of a pet dog or cat.

Isolation can lead to Despair

Perhaps there is no story that demonstrates so clearly the dangers of isolation as the story of Elijah. We know from the biblical book of I Kings, that Elijah was a fiery prophet of God.

He brought word from God to Ahab that there would be no rain and there was terrible drought for the next three and a half years. During that time, Elijah spent time in the wilderness and then with a widow in Zarephath.

The whole time, he was miraculously fed through God’s power, first by ravens and then through God’s provision of flour and oil to a widow, with whom he lived. Through God’s power, he raised the widow’s son to life.

Then came a time when he challenged the prophets of Baal to a match on Mt. Carmel and won a decisive victory for God. Miraculous fire descended from heaven in answer to his prayer. Truly, God was working great things in his life.

Very soon though, Elijah was running for his life into the desert. Jezebel had threatened his life and rather than trusting God, he fled to Mt. Horeb where he heard the voice of God.

When God asked him what he was doing there, Elijah replied, …I have been very jealous for the LORD God of hosts: for the children of Israel have forsaken thy covenant, thrown down thine altars, and slain thy prophets with the sword; and I, even I only, am left; and they seek my life, to take it away –1 Kings 19:10.

We can see here a big reason for Elijah’s weakness. He felt completely alone. God corrected Elijah’s incorrect assumption when He stated: Yet I have left me seven thousand in Israel, all the knees which have not bowed unto Baal, and every mouth which hath not kissed him –1 Kings 19:18.

The fact that those men and women existed in Israel did Elijah little good since he didn’t spend time with them. Elijah’s isolation led him to weakness and despair.

The story of Paul comes to mind as well. The Apostle Paul was a man who seemed to have nearly limitless amounts of energy and an unquenchable zeal for the things of God, but his last letter to Timothy from prison revealed a man who felt very alone. Do thy diligence to come shortly unto me: For Demas hath forsaken me, having loved this present world, and is departed unto Thessalonica; Crescens to Galatia, Titus unto Dalmatia. Only Luke is with me. Take Mark, and bring him with thee… –2 Timothy 4:9-11.

The Apostle was not abandoned. Other than Demas, they had not fled because they were afraid or ashamed of his bonds. He had sent many of his friends away to strengthen the church in various parts of the Roman Empire. Yet, Paul was still feeling isolated and needed the good Christian brothers, Timothy and Mark, to come and encourage him as he faced a martyr’s death.

Isolation is Physically Harmful

Studies have showed that isolation is linked to higher rates of high blood pressure, heart disease, anxiety, and depression. Older people who are isolated often show signs of mental decline and can experience worsening dementia.

Many times, as people age, they experience the deaths of loved ones. The loss of a spouse can lead older people to withdraw from others and to experience loneliness and isolation. This in turn often leads to rapid progression of the aging process.

Science does not fully understand it, but loneliness leads to increased inflammation and poorer immune function. This in turn can lead to lonely people getting worse infections and struggling to recover after such an infection.

While we think of these problems as those that primarily affect elderly people, they can affect younger people as well. In younger people, often loneliness doesn’t lead to memory issues, but it certainly can lead to things like depression, and it can make chronic inflammatory diseases much worse.

The Opposite of Isolation

If asked what the opposite of isolation is most people would probably answer “Companionship” or maybe even “Friendship”. There is another word which has a Christian connotation that is even better. That word is fellowship.

The Greek word translated fellowship in the New Testament is “Koinonia” and in the Bible it speaks of relationships that are founded on a shared love for God and for the church—a unity of belief and desire. Christian fellowship includes concepts like praying together, encouraging one another, and even suffering together.

I am afraid that many today find themselves in one of two dangerous situations. First, they may not be a member of any church congregation. While this may be unavoidable in certain mission outreach situations, it is not ideal, and most certainly it should not be a normal situation. At the very least it can create a sense of isolation, and at the worst it hinders many of the “one-anothering” Bible passages from being followed. We need fellowship, both to encourage us and to keep us accountable.

The second dangerous situation is that many believers, while members of a church, isolate themselves within that church. If you are a member of a large church congregation, it is easy to blend in and not develop relationships with others. This is just as harmful as not being a member of a church body. Too many people feel lonely, even when there are lots of people around.

Scripture makes it clear that we need a church body. Not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as the manner of some is; but exhorting one another: and so much the more, as ye see the day approaching –Hebrews 10:25.

There are many people who have lives that are full of friends and acquaintances, but if they do not have a place where they receive fellowship, they are missing out.

When I see people in my office who are struggling with depression there are two things I always tell them to do for themselves.

First is to start exercising. There have been several studies that compared exercise to antidepressants and found that it had similar effectiveness to many of the commonly prescribed antidepressant medications. This doesn’t have to be really vigorous exercise, but it does need to be aerobic (enough to raise the heart rate) and consistent.

The second is to become active in a church congregation; it is not enough to just attend church. Having brothers and sisters to pray for someone who is struggling, to listen to the discouraging situations, and to encourage that person to a more vibrant walk with God is really helpful.

Unfortunately, when someone is struggling with depression, the last thing they seem to want to do is make the effort to be around other people, which contrary to their feelings, is counterproductive to changing the problem.

As we consider this, it should move us to reach out to those who we know are struggling with isolation.

When someone loses a spouse, they often have a lot of encouragement for the first several weeks, but we need to make certain that they continue to have an active presence in their lives in the months that follow.

For every man shall bear his own burden –Galatians 6:5, should not give us excuse to not obey God’s command to Bear ye one another's burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ –Galatians 6:2. The family of God is given no time limit on bearing burdens. There is only a mandate that as we see our brother or sister struggling, we are to help them, as we are able.

The blessing is that someday, when we are struggling, we will have men and women of faith around us to encourage us and to pray for us. We cannot carry these burdens alone. Together, we will reach the Celestial City.

Isolation comes for many reasons. Sometimes it seems to be a chosen way of life, as is the natural tendency of introverted people. Sometimes it is foisted upon a person due to deaths of loved ones or other significant losses. Either way, it is not a healthy place to live.

As we find ourselves in these situations, we need to reach out for fellowship. The family of God is there for us if we only reach out.

As we see others who are struggling, we need to extend to them the right arm of fellowship. As we do so, we may, through our small efforts, help someone emotionally, physically, and spiritually, simply by being a friend in a time of isolation.

Over de hele wereld, maar met name in de Verenigde Staten, lijken mensen ruwe individualiteit te waarderen. Mensen die dit karaktertrekje tonen banen hun eigen weg door het leven, vragen niets van anderen en verwachten niets.

Ik veronderstel dat dit idee teruggaat naar de pioniers. Dit waren mannen en vrouwen die door verschillende nieuwe gebieden trokken op zoek naar een plek waar ze zich konden vestigen en die thuis noemen. Er waren weinig kruidenierswinkels en zoveel als mogelijk leefden ze zo zelfvoorzienend als ze konden.

Hoewel dit misschien klinkt als een scenario dat kracht uitstraalt, is de waarheid tegenwoordig enigszins anders. Tegenwoordig gebruiken mensen technologie om doelbewust bubbels van isolement om zich heen te creëren.

Veel oudere mensen hebben zich steeds meer geïsoleerd van vrienden en familie gevoeld. COVID heeft dit zeker verergerd, maar er waren zaden van deze afzondering die al lang vóór COVID waren gezaaid.

Isolement is geen natuurlijke toestand

Als we terugkijken naar de Hof van Eden zien we dat Adam vóór Eva werd geschapen. Hoewel er veel dieren aanwezig waren, was er geen echte metgezel voor Adam. En de HEERE God zeide: Het is niet goed dat de mens alleen zij; Ik zal hem een hulpbehoevende maken tegenover hem … En Adam gaf namen aan al het vee en aan de gevogelte des hemels en aan alle dieren des velds; maar voor Adam werd geen hulpbehoevende gevonden –Genesis 2:18-20.

En de HEERE God deed een diepen slaap vallen op Adam, en hij sliep; hij nam een van zijn ribben en sloot het vlees daar ter plaatse. En de rib, die de HEERE God van de mens genomen had, maakte Hij tot een vrouw en bracht haar tot de mens –Genesis 2:21-22. Natuurlijk was dit het begin van het huwelijk, maar het belangrijkere om hier te zien is dat het geen normale toestand is voor mensen om alleen te zijn. Wij verlangen naar gezelschap en niet alleen het gezelschap van een huisdier hond of kat.

Isolement kan tot wanhoop leiden

Waarschijnlijk is er geen verhaal dat de gevaren van isolement zo duidelijk aantoont als het verhaal van Elia. We weten uit het bijbelse boek I Koningen dat Elia een vurige profeet van God was.

Hij bracht van God de boodschap aan Achab dat er geen regen zou komen en er was een vreselijke droogte gedurende de daaropvolgende anderhalf jaar. Gedurende die tijd verbleef Elia in de woestijn en daarna bij een weduwe in Sarefat.

De hele tijd werd hij miraculeus gevoed door Gods macht, eerst door raven en daarna door Gods voorziening van meel en olie aan een weduwe bij wie hij woonde. Door Gods kracht wekte hij de zoon van de weduwe weer tot leven.

Toen kwam er een tijd dat hij de profeten van Baäl uitdaagde tot een duel op de berg Carmel en een beslissende overwinning voor God behaalde. Miraculeus vuur daalde uit de hemel als antwoord op zijn gebed. Waarlijk, God werkte grote dingen in zijn leven.

Maar zeer spoedig vluchtte Elia voor zijn leven de woestijn in. Izebel had zijn leven bedreigd en in plaats van God te vertrouwen, vluchtte hij naar de berg Horeb waar hij de stem van God hoorde.

Toen God hem vroeg wat hij daar deed, antwoordde Elia, …Ik heb zeer ijverig geweest voor de HEERE, de God der heirscharen; want de kinderen Israëls hebben Uw verbond verlaten, Uw altaren afgebroken en Uw profeten met het zwaard gedood; en ik, ik alleen, ben overgebleven; en zij zoeken mijn leven om het weg te nemen –1 Koningen 19:10.

We zien hier een grote reden voor Elia’s zwakte. Hij voelde zich volkomen alleen. God corrigeerde Elia’s foutieve aanname toen Hij zei: Doch Ik heb in Israël zevenduizend overgehouden, al wie de knie niet gebogen heeft voor Baäl en iedere mond die hem niet gekust heeft –1 Koningen 19:18.

Het feit dat die mannen en vrouwen in Israël bestonden deed Elia weinig goed omdat hij geen tijd met hen had doorgebracht. Elia’s isolement leidde tot zwakte en wanhoop.

Ook het verhaal van Paulus komt bij me op. De apostel Paulus was een man die schijnbaar bijna onbeperkte energie had en een onverzadigbare ijver voor de dingen van God, maar zijn laatste brief aan Timoteüs uit de gevangenis toonde een man die zich zeer alleen voelde. Spaar niet en kom gauw tot mij; want Demas heeft mij verlaten, omdat hij de tegenwoordige wereld liefgekregen heeft, en is vertrokken naar Thessalonica; Crescens naar Galatië, Titus naar Dalmatia. Lucas alleen is bij mij. Neem Markus en breng hem mede… –2 Timoteüs 4:9-11.

De apostel was niet in de steek gelaten. Afgezien van Demas waren ze niet gevlucht omdat ze bang of beschaamd waren over zijn boeien. Hij had veel van zijn vrienden weggestuurd om de kerk in verschillende delen van het Romeinse Rijk te versterken. Toch voelde Paulus zich geïsoleerd en had hij de goede christelijke broeders Timoteüs en Markus nodig om te komen en hem aan te moedigen terwijl hij een marteldood tegemoet zag.

Isolement is lichamelijk schadelijk

Studies hebben aangetoond dat isolement wordt gekoppeld aan hogere percentages hoge bloeddruk, hartziekten, angst en depressie. Oudere mensen die geïsoleerd zijn tonen vaak tekenen van mentale achteruitgang en kunnen verergerende dementie ervaren.

Vaak ervaren mensen naarmate ze ouder worden de dood van geliefden. Het verlies van een echtgenoot kan ertoe leiden dat oudere mensen zich terugtrekken van anderen en eenzaamheid en isolement ervaren. Dit leidt op zijn beurt vaak tot een versnelde voortgang van het verouderingsproces.

De wetenschap begrijpt het niet volledig, maar eenzaamheid leidt tot verhoogde ontsteking en slechtere immuunfunctie. Dit kan er op zijn beurt toe leiden dat eenzame mensen ernstigere infecties krijgen en moeite hebben te herstellen na zo'n infectie.

Hoewel we deze problemen doorgaans zien als problemen die vooral ouderen treffen, kunnen ze ook jongeren treffen. Bij jongere mensen leidt eenzaamheid vaak niet tot geheugenproblemen, maar het kan zeker leiden tot zaken als depressie, en het kan chronische ontstekingsziekten veel erger maken.

Het tegenovergestelde van isolement

Als men zou vragen wat het tegenovergestelde van isolement is, zouden de meeste mensen waarschijnlijk antwoorden "gezelschap" of misschien zelfs "vriendschap". Er is een ander woord met een christelijke connotatie dat nog beter is. Dat woord is gemeenschap.

Het Griekse woord dat in het Nieuwe Testament met gemeenschap is vertaald is "koinonia" en in de Bijbel spreekt het van relaties die zijn gegrondvest op een gedeelde liefde voor God en voor de kerk—een eenheid van geloof en verlangen. Christelijke gemeenschap omvat concepten als samen bidden, elkaar bemoedigen en zelfs samen lijden.

Ik ben bang dat velen zich vandaag in een van twee gevaarlijke situaties bevinden. Ten eerste: zij zijn misschien geen lid van enige kerkelijke gemeente. Hoewel dit in bepaalde zendingssituaties onvermijdelijk kan zijn, is het niet ideaal en zeker geen normale situatie. Op zijn minst kan het een gevoel van isolement scheppen, en in het ergste geval verhindert het dat veel van de "plicht-aan-elkaar" Bijbelpassages worden nagevolgd. We hebben gemeenschap nodig, zowel om ons aan te moedigen als om ons ter verantwoording te houden.

De tweede gevaarlijke situatie is dat veel gelovigen, hoewel ze lid zijn van een kerk, zich binnen die kerk isoleren. Als je lid bent van een grote gemeente, is het makkelijk om op te gaan in de massa en geen relaties met anderen te ontwikkelen. Dit is net zo schadelijk als geen lid zijn van een kerkelijk lichaam. Te veel mensen voelen zich eenzaam, zelfs wanneer er veel mensen om hen heen zijn.

De Schrift maakt duidelijk dat we een kerkelijk lichaam nodig hebben. En laten wij onze samenscholing niet nalaten, zoals sommigen gewoonlijk doen, maar elkaar vermanen, en dat des te meer naarmate gij de dag ziet naderen –Hebreeën 10:25.

Er zijn veel mensen die levens vol vrienden en kennissen hebben, maar als zij geen plek hebben waar zij gemeenschap ontvangen, dan ontbreken zij iets essentieels.

Wanneer ik mensen in mijn spreekkamer zie die worstelen met depressie, zeg ik altijd twee dingen die ze voor zichzelf moeten doen.

De eerste is te beginnen met lichaamsbeweging. Er zijn meerdere studies geweest die lichaamsbeweging vergeleken met antidepressiva en ontdekten dat het vergelijkbare effectiviteit had als veel van de veelvoorkomende voorgeschreven antidepressiva. Dit hoeft geen zeer intensieve inspanning te zijn, maar het moet wel aerobisch zijn (genoeg om de hartslag te verhogen) en consequent.

Het tweede is actief te worden in een kerkelijke gemeente; alleen naar de kerk gaan is niet genoeg. Broeders en zusters hebben voor iemand die worstelt te bidden, naar ontmoedigende situaties te luisteren en die persoon aan te moedigen tot een levendiger wandel met God is werkelijk behulpzaam.

Helaas, als iemand worstelt met depressie, lijkt het laatste wat zij willen doen juist de moeite te nemen om bij andere mensen in de buurt te zijn, wat in tegenstelling tot hun gevoelens contraproductief is voor het oplossen van het probleem.

Als we hierover nadenken, zou het ons ertoe moeten aanzetten om degenen te benaderen waarvan we weten dat ze worstelen met isolement.

Wanneer iemand een echtgenoot verliest, hebben zij vaak veel bemoediging gedurende de eerste weken, maar we moeten ervoor zorgen dat zij in de maanden die volgen een actieve aanwezigheid in hun leven blijven houden.

Want ieder zal zijn eigen last dragen –Galaten 6:5, mag ons geen excuus geven om Gods gebod niet te gehoorzamen: Draagt elkanders lasten, en vervult alzo de wet van Christus –Galaten 6:2. De familie van God krijgt geen tijdslimiet opgelegd voor het dragen van lasten. Er is alleen een gebod dat als we onze broeder of zuster zien worstelen, wij hen moeten helpen, zoals wij daartoe in staat zijn.

De zegen is dat op een dag, wanneer wij worstelen, er mannen en vrouwen des geloofs om ons heen zullen zijn om ons aan te moedigen en voor ons te bidden. Wij kunnen deze lasten niet alleen dragen. Gezamenlijk zullen wij de Hemelse Stad bereiken.

Isolement ontstaat om vele redenen. Soms lijkt het een gekozen manier van leven te zijn, zoals de natuurlijke neiging van introverte mensen. Soms wordt het iemand opgedrongen door de dood van geliefden of andere belangrijke verliezen. Hoe dan ook, het is geen gezonde plaats om te leven.

Wanneer we ons in deze situaties bevinden, moeten we ons uitstrekken naar gemeenschap. De familie van God is daar voor ons als we ons maar uitstrekken.

Wanneer we anderen zien worstelen, moeten we hun de rechterhand van gemeenschap aanbieden. Door dat te doen, kunnen we door onze kleine inspanningen iemand emotioneel, lichamelijk en geestelijk helpen, simpelweg door een vriend te zijn in een tijd van isolement.

Around the world, but particularly in the United States, people seem to value rugged individualism. People who demonstrate this character quality make their own way through life, asking nothing from others and expecting nothing.

I suppose that this idea relates back to the pioneers. These were men and women who trekked across the various new countries looking for a place where they could settle down and call home. There were few general stores and as much as possible they lived as self-sufficiently as they could.

While this may sound like a scenario that demonstrates strength, the truth is somewhat different these days. These days people use technology to deliberately create bubbles of isolation around themselves.

Many older people have found themselves increasingly isolated from friends and family. COVID certainly made this worse, but there were seeds of this seclusion that had been sowed long before COVID was ever heard of.

Isolation is Not a Natural State

Looking back to the Garden of Eden we can see that Adam was created before Eve. While there were lots of animals around, there was no true companionship for Adam. And the LORD God said, It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him … And Adam gave names to all cattle, and to the fowl of the air, and to every beast of the field; but for Adam there was not found an help meet for him –Genesis 2:18-20.

And the LORD God caused a deep sleep to fall upon Adam, and he slept: and he took one of his ribs, and closed up the flesh instead thereof; And the rib, which the LORD God had taken from man, made he a woman, and brought her unto the man –Genesis 2:21-22. Of course, this was the beginning of marriage, but the more important thing to see here is that it is not a normal state for humans to be alone. We desire companionship and not just the companionship of a pet dog or cat.

Isolation can lead to Despair

Perhaps there is no story that demonstrates so clearly the dangers of isolation as the story of Elijah. We know from the biblical book of I Kings, that Elijah was a fiery prophet of God.

He brought word from God to Ahab that there would be no rain and there was terrible drought for the next three and a half years. During that time, Elijah spent time in the wilderness and then with a widow in Zarephath.

The whole time, he was miraculously fed through God’s power, first by ravens and then through God’s provision of flour and oil to a widow, with whom he lived. Through God’s power, he raised the widow’s son to life.

Then came a time when he challenged the prophets of Baal to a match on Mt. Carmel and won a decisive victory for God. Miraculous fire descended from heaven in answer to his prayer. Truly, God was working great things in his life.

Very soon though, Elijah was running for his life into the desert. Jezebel had threatened his life and rather than trusting God, he fled to Mt. Horeb where he heard the voice of God.

When God asked him what he was doing there, Elijah replied, …I have been very jealous for the LORD God of hosts: for the children of Israel have forsaken thy covenant, thrown down thine altars, and slain thy prophets with the sword; and I, even I only, am left; and they seek my life, to take it away –1 Kings 19:10.

We can see here a big reason for Elijah’s weakness. He felt completely alone. God corrected Elijah’s incorrect assumption when He stated: Yet I have left me seven thousand in Israel, all the knees which have not bowed unto Baal, and every mouth which hath not kissed him –1 Kings 19:18.

The fact that those men and women existed in Israel did Elijah little good since he didn’t spend time with them. Elijah’s isolation led him to weakness and despair.

The story of Paul comes to mind as well. The Apostle Paul was a man who seemed to have nearly limitless amounts of energy and an unquenchable zeal for the things of God, but his last letter to Timothy from prison revealed a man who felt very alone. Do thy diligence to come shortly unto me: For Demas hath forsaken me, having loved this present world, and is departed unto Thessalonica; Crescens to Galatia, Titus unto Dalmatia. Only Luke is with me. Take Mark, and bring him with thee… –2 Timothy 4:9-11.

The Apostle was not abandoned. Other than Demas, they had not fled because they were afraid or ashamed of his bonds. He had sent many of his friends away to strengthen the church in various parts of the Roman Empire. Yet, Paul was still feeling isolated and needed the good Christian brothers, Timothy and Mark, to come and encourage him as he faced a martyr’s death.

Isolation is Physically Harmful

Studies have showed that isolation is linked to higher rates of high blood pressure, heart disease, anxiety, and depression. Older people who are isolated often show signs of mental decline and can experience worsening dementia.

Many times, as people age, they experience the deaths of loved ones. The loss of a spouse can lead older people to withdraw from others and to experience loneliness and isolation. This in turn often leads to rapid progression of the aging process.

Science does not fully understand it, but loneliness leads to increased inflammation and poorer immune function. This in turn can lead to lonely people getting worse infections and struggling to recover after such an infection.

While we think of these problems as those that primarily affect elderly people, they can affect younger people as well. In younger people, often loneliness doesn’t lead to memory issues, but it certainly can lead to things like depression, and it can make chronic inflammatory diseases much worse.

The Opposite of Isolation

If asked what the opposite of isolation is most people would probably answer “Companionship” or maybe even “Friendship”. There is another word which has a Christian connotation that is even better. That word is fellowship.

The Greek word translated fellowship in the New Testament is “Koinonia” and in the Bible it speaks of relationships that are founded on a shared love for God and for the church—a unity of belief and desire. Christian fellowship includes concepts like praying together, encouraging one another, and even suffering together.

I am afraid that many today find themselves in one of two dangerous situations. First, they may not be a member of any church congregation. While this may be unavoidable in certain mission outreach situations, it is not ideal, and most certainly it should not be a normal situation. At the very least it can create a sense of isolation, and at the worst it hinders many of the “one-anothering” Bible passages from being followed. We need fellowship, both to encourage us and to keep us accountable.

The second dangerous situation is that many believers, while members of a church, isolate themselves within that church. If you are a member of a large church congregation, it is easy to blend in and not develop relationships with others. This is just as harmful as not being a member of a church body. Too many people feel lonely, even when there are lots of people around.

Scripture makes it clear that we need a church body. Not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as the manner of some is; but exhorting one another: and so much the more, as ye see the day approaching –Hebrews 10:25.

There are many people who have lives that are full of friends and acquaintances, but if they do not have a place where they receive fellowship, they are missing out.

When I see people in my office who are struggling with depression there are two things I always tell them to do for themselves.

First is to start exercising. There have been several studies that compared exercise to antidepressants and found that it had similar effectiveness to many of the commonly prescribed antidepressant medications. This doesn’t have to be really vigorous exercise, but it does need to be aerobic (enough to raise the heart rate) and consistent.

The second is to become active in a church congregation; it is not enough to just attend church. Having brothers and sisters to pray for someone who is struggling, to listen to the discouraging situations, and to encourage that person to a more vibrant walk with God is really helpful.

Unfortunately, when someone is struggling with depression, the last thing they seem to want to do is make the effort to be around other people, which contrary to their feelings, is counterproductive to changing the problem.

As we consider this, it should move us to reach out to those who we know are struggling with isolation.

When someone loses a spouse, they often have a lot of encouragement for the first several weeks, but we need to make certain that they continue to have an active presence in their lives in the months that follow.

For every man shall bear his own burden –Galatians 6:5, should not give us excuse to not obey God’s command to Bear ye one another's burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ –Galatians 6:2. The family of God is given no time limit on bearing burdens. There is only a mandate that as we see our brother or sister struggling, we are to help them, as we are able.

The blessing is that someday, when we are struggling, we will have men and women of faith around us to encourage us and to pray for us. We cannot carry these burdens alone. Together, we will reach the Celestial City.

Isolation comes for many reasons. Sometimes it seems to be a chosen way of life, as is the natural tendency of introverted people. Sometimes it is foisted upon a person due to deaths of loved ones or other significant losses. Either way, it is not a healthy place to live.

As we find ourselves in these situations, we need to reach out for fellowship. The family of God is there for us if we only reach out.

As we see others who are struggling, we need to extend to them the right arm of fellowship. As we do so, we may, through our small efforts, help someone emotionally, physically, and spiritually, simply by being a friend in a time of isolation.

In tutto il mondo, ma particolarmente negli Stati Uniti, la gente sembra apprezzare l'individualismo duro e tenace. Le persone che dimostrano questa qualità caratteriale si fanno strada nella vita da sole, non chiedendo nulla agli altri e aspettandosi nulla.

Suppongo che questa idea risalga ai pionieri. Erano uomini e donne che attraversarono i vari nuovi territori in cerca di un luogo dove stabilirsi e poter chiamare casa. C'erano pochi negozi generali e, per quanto possibile, vivevano in modo il più autosufficiente possibile.

Sebbene questo possa sembrare uno scenario che dimostra forza, la verità oggi è in parte diversa. Oggi le persone usano la tecnologia per creare deliberatamente bolle di isolamento intorno a sé.

Molti anziani si sono trovati sempre più isolati da amici e familiari. Il COVID ha sicuramente peggiorato la situazione, ma c'erano dei semi di questa segregazione che erano stati seminati molto prima che si sentisse parlare del COVID.

L'isolamento non è uno stato naturale

Guardando al Giardino dell'Eden possiamo vedere che Adamo fu creato prima di Eva. Pur essendoci molti animali intorno, non c'era una vera compagnia per Adamo. E il SIGNORE Dio disse: Non è bene che l'uomo sia solo; gli farò un aiuto adatto a lui … E Adamo diede nomi a tutto il bestiame, agli uccelli del cielo e a tutte le bestie dei campi; ma per Adamo non si trovò un aiuto adatto a lui –Genesi 2:18-20.

E il SIGNORE Dio fece cadere un profondo sonno su Adamo, che si addormentò; poi prese una delle sue costole e chiuse la carne al suo posto; E dalla costola che il SIGNORE Dio aveva tolto all'uomo formò una donna e la condusse all'uomo –Genesi 2:21-22. Naturalmente, questo fu l'inizio del matrimonio, ma la cosa più importante da vedere qui è che non è uno stato normale per gli esseri umani essere soli. Desideriamo compagnia e non solo la compagnia di un cane o di un gatto domestico.

L'isolamento può portare alla disperazione

Forse non c'è storia che dimostri così chiaramente i pericoli dell'isolamento come la storia di Elia. Sappiamo dal libro biblico dei Re che Elia fu un profeta ardente di Dio.

Portò da Dio a Acab il messaggio che non ci sarebbe stata pioggia e ci fu una terribile siccità per i successivi tre anni e mezzo. Durante quel tempo, Elia trascorse del tempo nel deserto e poi con una vedova a Sarepta.

Per tutto il tempo fu nutrito miracolosamente per potere di Dio, prima dai corvi e poi mediante la provvidenza di Dio che fornì farina e olio a una vedova, con la quale abitò. Per potere di Dio risuscitò il figlio della vedova.

Poi venne un tempo in cui sfidò i profeti di Baal a una contesa sul monte Carmelo e vinse una vittoria decisiva per Dio. Fuoco miracoloso discese dal cielo in risposta alla sua preghiera. Davvero, Dio stava operando grandi cose nella sua vita.

Molto presto però, Elia fuggì per la sua vita nel deserto. Iezabele aveva minacciato la sua vita e invece di confidare in Dio, fuggì sul monte Oreb dove udì la voce di Dio.

Quando Dio gli chiese cosa stesse facendo lì, Elia rispose, …io sono stato molto geloso per il SIGNORE Dio degli eserciti: perché i figli d'Israele hanno abbandonato il tuo patto, hanno rovesciato i tuoi altari e hanno ucciso i tuoi profeti a fil di spada; e io, io solo, sono rimasto; e cercano la mia vita per togliermela –1 Re 19:10.

Vediamo qui una grande ragione della debolezza di Elia. Si sentiva completamente solo. Dio corregge l'errata supposizione di Elia quando dice: Eppure io ho risparmiato in Israele settemila persone, tutte le ginocchia che non si sono piegate a Baal e tutte le bocche che non l'hanno baciato –1 Re 19:18.

Il fatto che quegli uomini e quelle donne esistessero in Israele servì a poco a Elia poiché egli non trascorreva del tempo con loro. L'isolamento di Elia lo portò a debolezza e disperazione.

Viene in mente anche la storia di Paolo. L'apostolo Paolo era un uomo che pareva avere quantità quasi illimitate di energia e uno zelo inesauribile per le cose di Dio, ma la sua ultima lettera a Timoteo dalla prigione rivelò un uomo che si sentiva molto solo. Fai presto a venire da me: perché Demas mi ha abbandonato, avendo amato questo presente mondo, ed è partito per Tessalonica; Crescenzio per la Galazia, Tito per la Dalmazia. Solo Luca è con me. Prendi Marco e portalo con te… –2 Timoteo 4:9-11.

L'apostolo non era abbandonato. Fuori da Demas, non se ne erano andati perché avevano paura o si vergognavano delle sue catene. Egli aveva mandato molti dei suoi amici in varie parti dell'impero romano per rafforzare la chiesa. Eppure Paolo si sentiva comunque isolato e aveva bisogno dei buoni fratelli cristiani, Timoteo e Marco, affinché venissero a incoraggiarlo mentre affrontava una morte da martire.

L'isolamento è dannoso fisicamente

Studi hanno dimostrato che l'isolamento è collegato a tassi più elevati di ipertensione, malattie cardiache, ansia e depressione. Gli anziani isolati mostrano spesso segni di declino mentale e possono sperimentare un peggioramento della demenza.

Molte volte, con l'avanzare dell'età, si sperimentano le morti di persone care. La perdita del coniuge può portare gli anziani a ritirarsi dagli altri e a provare solitudine e isolamento. Questo a sua volta spesso conduce a un rapido avanzamento del processo d'invecchiamento.

La scienza non lo comprende completamente, ma la solitudine porta a un aumento dell'infiammazione e a una funzione immunitaria peggiorata. Questo a sua volta può portare le persone sole a contrarre infezioni più gravi e ad avere difficoltà a recuperare dopo tali infezioni.

Pur pensando a questi problemi come principalmente legati agli anziani, essi possono colpire anche i più giovani. Nei giovani, spesso la solitudine non porta a problemi di memoria, ma certamente può portare a cose come la depressione e può peggiorare molto le malattie infiammatorie croniche.

Il contrario dell'isolamento

Se chiesto quale sia il contrario dell'isolamento, la maggior parte delle persone probabilmente risponderebbe “compagnia” o magari anche “amicizia”. C'è un'altra parola che ha una connotazione cristiana ed è ancora migliore. Quella parola è comunione.

La parola greca tradotta con comunione nel Nuovo Testamento è “Koinonia” e nella Bibbia parla di relazioni fondate su un amore condiviso per Dio e per la chiesa—una unità di fede e desiderio. La comunione cristiana include concetti come pregare insieme, esortarsi a vicenda e persino soffrire insieme.

Temo che oggi molti si trovino in una di due situazioni pericolose. Prima, possono non essere membri di alcuna congregazione ecclesiale. Pur essendo talvolta inevitabile in certe situazioni di missione, non è l'ideale e certamente non dovrebbe essere una situazione normale. Al minimo può creare un senso di isolamento, e al peggio ostacola molte delle istruzioni bibliche del tipo “l'un l'altro”. Abbiamo bisogno di comunione, sia per essere incoraggiati sia per essere resi responsabili.

La seconda situazione pericolosa è che molti credenti, pur essendo membri di una chiesa, si isolano all'interno di quella chiesa. Se sei membro di una grande congregazione, è facile confondersi nella massa e non sviluppare relazioni con gli altri. Questo è dannoso tanto quanto non essere membri di un corpo ecclesiale. Troppa gente si sente sola, anche quando ci sono molte persone intorno.

Le Scritture chiariscono che abbiamo bisogno di un corpo di chiesa. Non abbandonando la nostra comune adunanza, come alcuni sono soliti fare, ma esortandoci a vicenda; e tanto più, quanto vedete avvicinarsi il giorno –Ebrei 10:25.

Ci sono molte persone che hanno vite piene di amici e conoscenze, ma se non hanno un luogo dove ricevono comunione, stanno perdendo qualcosa di importante.

Quando vedo persone nel mio studio che lottano con la depressione, ci sono due cose che dico sempre loro di fare per il proprio bene.

La prima è iniziare a fare esercizio fisico. Ci sono stati diversi studi che hanno confrontato l'esercizio con gli antidepressivi e hanno trovato che ha un'efficacia simile a molti dei farmaci antidepressivi comunemente prescritti. Non deve essere esercizio molto vigoroso, ma deve essere aerobico (sufficiente ad aumentare la frequenza cardiaca) e consistente.

La seconda è diventare attivi in una congregazione ecclesiale; non basta semplicemente frequentare la chiesa. Avere fratelli e sorelle che pregano per chi sta lottando, che ascoltano le situazioni scoraggianti e che incoraggiano quella persona a una camminata più vibrante con Dio è davvero d'aiuto.

Sfortunatamente, quando qualcuno lotta con la depressione, l'ultima cosa che sembra volere è lo sforzo di stare vicino ad altre persone, il che, contrariamente ai loro sentimenti, è controproducente per il cambiamento del problema.

Mentre consideriamo questo, dovrebbe spingerci a tendere la mano a coloro che sappiamo stiano lottando con l'isolamento.

Quando qualcuno perde il coniuge, spesso riceve molto incoraggiamento per le prime settimane, ma dobbiamo assicurarci che continui ad avere una presenza attiva nella sua vita nei mesi successivi.

Perché ciascuno porterà il proprio carico –Galati 6:5, non dovrebbe darci la scusa per non obbedire al comando di Dio di Portate i pesi gli uni degli altri e così adempirete la legge di Cristo –Galati 6:2. Alla famiglia di Dio non è dato un limite di tempo per portare i pesi. C'è solo un mandato che, quando vediamo il nostro fratello o la nostra sorella in difficoltà, dobbiamo aiutarli, come siamo in grado.

La benedizione è che un giorno, quando noi stessi lotteremo, avremo uomini e donne di fede attorno a noi per incoraggiarci e pregare per noi. Non possiamo portare questi pesi da soli. Insieme raggiungeremo la Città Celeste.

L'isolamento arriva per molte ragioni. A volte sembra una scelta di vita, come è la tendenza naturale delle persone introverse. A volte è imposto a una persona a causa della morte di persone care o di altre perdite significative. In entrambi i casi, non è un luogo sano in cui vivere.

Quando ci troviamo in queste situazioni, dobbiamo cercare la comunione. La famiglia di Dio è lì per noi se solo tendiamo la mano.

Quando vediamo altri che stanno lottando, dobbiamo estendere loro il giusto braccio di comunione. Facendo così, con i nostri piccoli sforzi, potremmo aiutare qualcuno emotivamente, fisicamente e spiritualmente, semplicemente essendo un amico in un tempo di isolamento.

Ellie edged her chair closer to the grown-ups who were visiting in the kitchen. Grandpa, Grandma, and Aunt Lily had stopped by for a visit, and although she didn’t always understand the conversation, she loved to listen. She found that she learned a lot of things that way.

The topic this evening was about something related to church and that got her mind to thinking about singing during Sunday morning worship services. Although Ellie was only five years old, she very much loved to sing. She thought about the fact that her dear Grandpa was a song leader in their church and how much she liked when he led a song.

At Ellie’s church the song leaders all sat around a table near the center of the church. They took turns choosing a song and then leading it for the congregation. Ellie didn’t always know the songs that were chosen. They sang out of a little black hymnbook that had lots of songs with hard words and tunes she didn’t recognize. However, in the back of this little songbook was a section called “The Appendix” and here were hymns that were familiar to her and she was always pleased when a song was announced from that part of the book. Her favorite song was ‘Saviour, Like a Shepherd Lead Us’ and although she couldn’t read yet, she knew it was number eight. When that particular song number was announced on a Sunday morning, she always felt a twinge of excitement. She would be able to help along with this song!

I wish we would sing that song again, thought Ellie. It’s been a long time since we have.

Then a sudden thought struck her. Why couldn’t she ask Grandpa to choose that song next Sunday?

Yes, I will ask him and see what he says about that idea, she smiled to herself. She decided to wait until her grandparents were ready to leave. She followed Grandpa out the door and as he walked across the porch, she quickly stepped up next to him. “Grandpa,” she asked. “Do you think you could lead the song ‘Saviour, Like A Shepherd Lead Us’ this next Sunday? I would really like to sing it again!” She felt suddenly shy at having asked such a question, and she ducked back toward the doorway of the house.

Grandpa smiled down at her. “I think I can do that. Is that a song you like?” His eyes twinkled at Ellie. “I’ll be happy to lead that one just for you.”

Ellie could scarcely wait for church the following Sunday. She would get to sing “her” song. Grandpa said he would choose it and she had no doubt he would do as he said.

Sunday morning, she waited eagerly for the song service to begin. The first and second songs were ones that were not familiar to her. Then came time for the third one. “Let’s sing number 8 in the Appendix,” announced the song leader. Ellie’s heart sang. They were going to sing her favorite song. Her grandpa had honored her request. Her eyes shone as she joined in the singing of the beautiful song. It was a lovely hymn that spoke of Jesus’ care as a Shepherd and a Friend, and how He would always keep His children close to Himself.

Later, after church was over and they were on their way home, Ellie remarked to her mother, “Grandpa chose that one song, just like I asked him to!”

Ellie’s mom looked a bit startled. “You asked him to lead a song today? When did you ask him?”

“Yes, I did. The other evening when they visited, I asked him if he could lead it today and he said he would. And he did!” Ellie said with delight.

Mom had a strange look on her face, and she was quiet for a moment.

“Did you know that Grandpas weren’t there today? At the last minute they decided to visit elsewhere this morning for church.” Mom smiled tenderly at her little daughter. “It seems that God knew what a little girl’s heart was desiring and He led another brother to choose the song you like so much. That’s so amazing, isn’t it?” Ellie nodded. To think that Grandpa wasn’t even at church today, and still they sang her favorite song anyway! It gave her such a special feeling to know that Jesus cared for her that much.

Today, Ellie is a grown-up woman and now has children of her own. Whenever she thinks about how Jesus cares for all His children, she especially remembers how God cared about one little, five-year-old girl and the song she loved so much. As her mother said, and still does, “Of course God cares. He loves all the little children of the world!”

Blessed Jesus! blessed Jesus!
Thou hast bought us, Thine we are.
Blessed Jesus! blessed Jesus!
Thou hast bought us, Thine we are.

We are Thine, do Thou befriend us,
Be the guardian of our way.
Keep Thy flock, from sin defend us,
Seek us when we go astray:
Blessed Jesus! blessed Jesus!
Hear, O hear us when we pray.
Blessed Jesus! blessed Jesus!
Hear, O hear us when we pray.

Thou hast promised to receive us,
Poor and sinful though we be.
Thou hast mercy to relieve us,
Grace to cleanse, and pow’r to free:
Blessed Jesus! blessed Jesus!
Early let us turn to Thee.
Blessed Jesus! blessed Jesus!
Early let us turn to Thee.

Early let us seek Thy favor,
Early let us do Thy will.
Blessed Lord and only Savior,
With Thy love our bosoms fill:
Blessed Jesus! blessed Jesus!
Thou hast loved us, love us still.
Blessed Jesus! blessed Jesus!
Thou hast loved us, love us still.

Dorothy Ann Thrupp

Ellie menggeser kursinya mendekat kepada orang dewasa yang sedang berkunjung di dapur. Kakek, Nenek, dan Bibi Lily mampir untuk berkunjung, dan meskipun dia tidak selalu mengerti percakapan itu, dia senang mendengarkan. Dia menemukan bahwa dia belajar banyak hal dengan cara itu.

Topik malam itu berkaitan dengan sesuatu tentang gereja dan itu membuat pikirannya memikirkan lagu saat kebaktian Minggu pagi. Meskipun Ellie baru berumur lima tahun, dia sangat suka bernyanyi. Dia memikirkan kenyataan bahwa Kakeknya yang tercinta adalah pemimpin nyanyian di gereja mereka dan betapa dia suka ketika kakeknya memimpin sebuah lagu.

Di gereja Ellie para pemimpin nyanyian semua duduk di sekitar meja di dekat tengah gereja. Mereka bergiliran memilih lagu dan kemudian memimpinnya untuk jemaat. Ellie tidak selalu tahu lagu-lagu yang dipilih. Mereka bernyanyi dari sebuah buku himne kecil berwarna hitam yang berisi banyak lagu dengan kata-kata sulit dan melodi yang tidak dikenalnya. Namun, di bagian belakang buku nyanyian kecil itu ada bagian yang disebut “Lampiran” dan di sana ada himne-himne yang familier baginya dan dia selalu senang ketika sebuah lagu diumumkan dari bagian itu. Lagu favoritnya adalah ‘Saviour, Like a Shepherd Lead Us’ dan meskipun dia belum bisa membaca, dia tahu itu nomor delapan. Ketika nomor lagu itu diumumkan pada pagi Minggu, dia selalu merasakan kegembiraan kecil. Dia akan bisa membantu menyanyikan lagu ini!

Andai kami menyanyikan lagu itu lagi, pikir Ellie. Sudah lama sejak terakhir kali kami menyanyikannya.

Lalu sebuah pikiran tiba-tiba menyambar benaknya. Mengapa dia tidak bisa meminta Kakek memilih lagu itu Minggu depan?

Ya, aku akan menanyakannya padanya dan lihat apa kata dia tentang gagasan itu, dia tersenyum pada dirinya sendiri. Dia memutuskan menunggu sampai kakek-neneknya siap pergi. Dia mengikuti Kakek keluar pintu dan saat dia berjalan melintasi beranda, dia cepat-cepat melangkah di sampingnya. “Kakek,” tanyanya. “Apakah Kakek kira-kira bisa memimpin lagu ‘Saviour, Like A Shepherd Lead Us’ Minggu depan? Aku sangat ingin menyanyikannya lagi!” Dia tiba-tiba merasa malu telah mengajukan pertanyaan seperti itu, dan dia menunduk kembali menuju ambang pintu rumah.

Kakek tersenyum menatapnya. “Aku pikir aku bisa melakukan itu. Apakah itu lagu yang kau suka?” Matanya berkilau pada Ellie. “Aku akan senang memimpin lagu itu hanya untukmu.”

Ellie hampir tidak sabar menunggu kebaktian Minggu berikutnya. Dia akan menyanyikan “lagunya”. Kakek mengatakan dia akan memilihnya dan dia yakin kakeknya akan menepati kata-katanya.

Pagi Minggu, dia menunggu dengan bersemangat agar kebaktian nyanyian dimulai. Lagu pertama dan kedua adalah lagu-lagu yang tidak dikenalnya. Lalu tiba saat untuk lagu ketiga. “Mari kita nyanyikan nomor 8 di Lampiran,” umumkan pemimpin nyanyian. Hati Ellie bernyanyi. Mereka akan menyanyikan lagu favoritnya. Kakeknya memenuhi permintaannya. Matanya bersinar saat dia ikut menyanyikan lagu indah itu. Itu adalah himne yang indah yang berbicara tentang pemeliharaan Yesus sebagai Gembala dan Sahabat, dan bagaimana Dia akan selalu menjaga anak-anak-Nya dekat pada-Nya.

Beberapa saat kemudian, setelah kebaktian selesai dan mereka dalam perjalanan pulang, Ellie berkata kepada ibunya, “Kakek memilih lagu itu, persis seperti yang aku minta!”

Ibunya terlihat agak terkejut. “Kau memintanya untuk memimpin sebuah lagu hari ini? Kapan kau memintanya?”

“Ya, aku memintanya. Beberapa malam lalu ketika mereka berkunjung, aku menanyakan apakah dia bisa memimpinnya hari ini dan dia bilang dia akan melakukannya. Dan dia melakukannya!” kata Ellie dengan girang.

Ibu tampak memiliki wajah yang aneh, dan dia diam sejenak.

“Tahukah kau bahwa Kakek tidak ada di sana hari ini? Di menit terakhir mereka memutuskan beribadah di tempat lain pagi ini.” Ibu tersenyum lembut pada putrinya yang kecil. “Tampaknya Tuhan tahu apa yang diinginkan hati seorang anak kecil dan Dia menggerakkan seorang saudara lain untuk memilih lagu yang sangat kau sukai. Itu sangat menakjubkan, bukan?” Ellie mengangguk. Membayangkan bahwa Kakek bahkan tidak hadir di gereja hari itu, dan tetap saja mereka menyanyikan lagu favoritnya! Itu memberinya perasaan istimewa mengetahui bahwa Yesus peduli padanya sedemikian rupa.

Hari ini, Ellie adalah seorang wanita dewasa dan kini memiliki anak-anaknya sendiri. Setiap kali dia memikirkan bagaimana Yesus merawat semua anak-Nya, dia terutama ingat bagaimana Allah memperhatikan seorang gadis kecil berumur lima tahun dan lagu yang sangat dia cintai. Seperti yang dikatakan ibunya, dan masih dikatakan, “Tentu saja Tuhan peduli. Dia mencintai semua anak kecil di dunia!”

Ellie avvicinò la sedia a quella degli adulti che stavano facendo visita in cucina. Nonno, Nonna e zia Lily erano passati a trovarli e, anche se non capiva sempre la conversazione, a lei piaceva molto ascoltare. Scopriva così di imparare molte cose.

Quel pomeriggio l’argomento era qualcosa relativo alla chiesa e questo fece venire in mente a Ellie il canto durante il culto della domenica mattina. Anche se Ellie aveva solo cinque anni, amava moltissimo cantare. Pensò al fatto che il suo caro nonno era un conduttore dei canti nella loro chiesa e a quanto le piacesse quando guidava un inno.

Nella chiesa di Ellie i conduttori dei canti si sedevano tutti attorno a un tavolo vicino al centro della chiesa. Si alternavano nello scegliere un canto e poi nel dirigerlo per la congregazione. Ellie non conosceva sempre i canti che venivano scelti. Cantavano da un piccolo libro di inni nero che conteneva molti canti con parole difficili e melodie che a lei non suonavano familiari. Tuttavia, nella parte finale di quel piccolo libro c’era una sezione chiamata “Appendice” e lì c’erano inni che le erano familiari e si rallegrava sempre quando veniva annunciato un canto da quella parte del libro. Il suo canto preferito era «Salvatore, come un pastore guidaci» e, anche se non sapeva ancora leggere, sapeva che era il numero otto. Quando quel numero di canto veniva annunciato una domenica mattina, sentiva sempre un fremito di emozione. Avrei potuto dare una mano con questo canto!

Vorrei che cantassimo di nuovo quel canto, pensò Ellie. È passato molto tempo dall’ultima volta.

Poi le venne un’idea improvvisa. Perché non chiedere a Nonno di scegliere quel canto la prossima domenica?

Sì, glielo chiederò e vedrò cosa ne pensa, si sorrise. Decise di aspettare che i nonni fossero pronti per andarsene. Seguí Nonno fuori dalla porta e mentre lui camminava attraverso il portico, lei si affiancò rapidamente a lui. “Nonno,” chiese. “Pensi che potresti dirigere il canto ‘Salvatore, come un pastore guidaci’ questa prossima domenica? Mi piacerebbe davvero cantarlo di nuovo!” Si sentì improvvisamente timida per aver fatto quella domanda e si ritrasse verso l’ingresso della casa.

Nonno le sorrise affacciandosi su di lei. “Penso di poterlo fare. È un canto che ti piace?” I suoi occhi scintillarono verso Ellie. “Sarò felice di dirigere proprio quello solo per te.”

Ellie non vedeva l’ora che arrivasse la domenica successiva. Avrebbe potuto cantare “il suo” canto. Nonno aveva detto che l’avrebbe scelto e non aveva dubbi che avrebbe mantenuto la parola.

Domenica mattina, aspettò con impazienza che iniziasse il servizio dei canti. Il primo e il secondo canto erano quelli che non le erano familiari. Poi arrivò il momento del terzo. “Cantiamo il numero 8 nell’Appendice,” annunciò il conduttore dei canti. Il cuore di Ellie cantò. Avrebbero cantato il suo canto preferito. Suo nonno aveva esaudito la sua richiesta. Gli occhi le brillarono mentre si univa al canto del bellissimo inno. Era un inno soave che parlava della cura di Gesù come Pastore e Amico, e di come Egli avrebbe sempre tenuto i suoi figli vicino a sé.

Poco dopo, quando la chiesa era finita e stavano tornando a casa, Ellie disse a sua madre: “Nonno ha scelto proprio quel canto, proprio come gli ho chiesto!”

La mamma di Ellie sembrò un po’ sorpresa. “Gli hai chiesto di dirigere un canto oggi? Quando gliel’hai chiesto?”

“Sì, gliel’ho chiesto. L’altra sera, quando sono venuti in visita, gli ho chiesto se poteva dirigerlo oggi e lui ha detto che lo avrebbe fatto. E l’ha fatto!” disse Ellie con entusiasmo.

La mamma aveva un’espressione strana e rimase in silenzio per un momento.

“Lo sapevi che i nonni non c’erano oggi? All’ultimo momento hanno deciso di partecipare al culto altrove stamattina.” La mamma sorrise teneramente alla sua bambina. “Sembra che Dio abbia conosciuto il desiderio del cuore di una piccola bambina e abbia guidato un altro fratello a scegliere il canto che ti piace tanto. Non è straordinario?” Ellie annuì. Pensare che il Nonno non fosse nemmeno in chiesa quel giorno, eppure comunque hanno cantato il suo canto preferito! Le dava una sensazione speciale sapere che Gesù si prendeva cura di lei in quel modo.

Oggi Ellie è una donna adulta e ha dei figli suoi. Ogni volta che pensa a come Gesù si prende cura di tutti i suoi figli, ricorda in modo particolare come Dio si sia preso cura di una piccola bambina di cinque anni e del canto che amava tanto. Come ha detto sua madre, e continua a dire, “Certo che Dio si prende cura. Ama tutti i piccoli bambini del mondo!”

Salvatore, come un pastore guidaci
